title: Butternut Squash Soup
subtitle: Creamy coconut and spice
excerpt: A velvety blended soup of roasted butternut squash enriched with coconut milk and lifted by warm spices. Naturally vegan and gluten-free, it is one of the easiest crowd-pleasing soups to have in your repertoire.
sourceNotes: Butternut squash soup became a staple of British home cooking from the 1990s onwards as winter squash varieties became widely available. The pairing with coconut milk and warm spices reflects the broad influence of South and Southeast Asian flavours on modern British cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost and reheat gently, adding a splash of water if needed.
recipe.batchNotes: An ideal batch-cook recipe. Doubles easily in a large stockpot.

content.text: Cubing and softening the squash in the pot rather than roasting it first keeps this recipe quick and weeknight-friendly. If you have an extra 30 minutes, roasting the squash at 200C with olive oil before adding it to the pot deepens the flavour considerably.
Heat the olive oil in the stockpot over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until softened and starting to turn golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, and chilli flakes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add the butternut squash cubes and stir to coat in the spiced oil. Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 20 minutes until the squash is completely tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir to combine. Remove from the heat.
Blend in batches until completely smooth. Return to the pan and reheat gently. Season generously with salt.
Ladle into bowls. Drizzle with a little coconut milk and scatter over a pinch of chilli flakes if you like.

items.cause: Squash released a lot of moisture, or too much stock was added.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 to 8 minutes before blending.

items.cause: Squash was not fully tender when blended.
items.fix: Simmer 5 more minutes; squash should fall apart when pressed.

items.symptom: Coconut milk has split in the bowl.
items.cause: The soup was reheated at too high a temperature.
items.fix: Reheat gently over low heat and stir continuously.
